meta.title: Cafe Kosame | A small Japanese-style tearoom in Incheon
meta.description: Cafe Kosame is a small Japanese-style tearoom full of plants, tucked into a quiet lane in Guwol-dong, Incheon. Mitarashi dango, rich matcha and hojicha. Open 12–9 pm, closed Thursdays.

title: After a light rain,
a green tearoom down the lane
hero.lead: A few steps from the busy streets, in a quiet residential lane. Dango and matcha, served in a small room full of plants.
hero.imageAlt: Illustration of a tearoom full of plants and trailing vines under a glass roof, light rain outside

ki.label: Arriving
ki.heading: The name comes from a gentle rain
paras: Kosame (小雨) is Japanese for light rain. Like leaves after a gentle shower, time here feels quiet and fresh.

About ten minutes on foot from Arts Center Station on Incheon Line 1. Where the noise of the Rodeo shopping street fades, a tearoom of wooden furniture, green plants, bamboo blinds, a few books and a small terrace waits in a residential lane.
Visitors have been writing about it since 2019, and it has kept its doors open in the same spot ever since.
ki.note: The owner credits regular guests for keeping such a small shop going for years, and closes each year with a promise to keep to the basics.
ki.noteSource: Summary of a Cafe Kosame Instagram post, December 2024
ki.imageAlt: Illustration of potted plants on shelves and a stool by a sunny window

sho.label: Staying
sho.heading: A cup of tea, a skewer of dango
sho.intro: The menu centers on Japanese teas and dango. You order at a kiosk, and the owner makes each drink and dessert by hand.

mitarashi.name: Mitarashi dango
mitarashi.desc: A sweet-savory glaze of dark soy sauce and brown sugar, balanced with tsuyu and salt over a long run of trials.

figDango.name: Fig and red bean dango
figDango.desc: Ripe figs with smooth red bean paste.

matchaLatte.name: Matcha latte
matchaLatte.desc: The drink visitors mention most for its depth and aroma.

hojichaLatte.name: Hojicha latte
hojichaLatte.desc: The toasty aroma of roasted green tea.

sho.pairing: If it’s your first time, start with the classic mitarashi dango and an unsweetened drink like an Americano or cold brew.
notes: Dine in from a single skewer. Takeout starts at two.
Reviewers note the matcha is whisked by hand with a bamboo whisk.
Many visitors mention a side of cherry tomatoes pickled in Japanese plum.
Desserts are made in small batches each day.
sho.priceNote: Prices are from public listings as of October 2026 and may change.

ten.label: Looking back
ten.heading: “Do you like dango?”
paras: Taking orders, the owner often overhears guests asking each other this.
When someone who hesitated because they’d never tried dango hands back an empty plate, that is the best encouragement, the owner wrote.
ten.paraSource: Summary of a Cafe Kosame Instagram post, March 2026

voices.title: What local visitors mention most
voices.body: A calm, quiet room, an interior like a tearoom in a small Japanese town, rich matcha and chewy dango. Many say it’s an easy place to go alone.

voices.title: How it’s introduced to travelers
voices.body: Korea Visit, a Korea travel guide for international readers, calls it a little piece of Japan in Guwol-dong and a good spot for solo time. An English-language travel log app also lists it as a quiet Japanese-style cafe on the edge of Guwol-dong.

ten.caveatsTitle: Good to know before you go
caveats: It’s small, so groups of four or more may not find a table.
The restroom is outside the building.
Some find the prices high for the portion size.
ten.summaryNote: Summarized from public reviews on several platforms.

ketsu.label: Visiting
ketsu.heading: Today, down the lane
ketsu.lead: Doors open at noon. It suits a sunny afternoon as well as a rainy one. Just remember it’s closed on Thursdays.

info.desc: Special hours are posted on Instagram
About 10 minutes on foot from Arts Center Station, Incheon Line 1
No dedicated parking. Use a nearby public lot
Kiosk ordering, one item per person

faq.q: Is it a good place to go alone?
faq.a: Yes. Coming alone is what reviewers mention most. You can order a single skewer of dango when dining in.

faq.q: Can a group of four or more visit?
faq.a: The cafe notes that groups of four or more may sometimes not find a table because the room is small. Quieter hours work best.

faq.q: Can I take dango to go?
faq.a: Takeout starts at two skewers. Single-skewer packaging is in the works.
Pets haven’t been allowed inside since March 1, 2026, due to new facility rules.

faq.q: Which map app should I use in Korea?
faq.a: Google Maps may not show walking routes in Korea. Naver Map or KakaoMap is the safer choice.

ketsu.closing: After the rain, step into the green tearoom down the lane.
